html:
On 16 February 1918 the twenty members of the Council of Lithuania, meeting in Vilnius, signed a declaration restoring an independent Lithuanian state. 16 February is the national day.

Lithuania was then occupied by Germany, which wanted it as a dependent state. The council, led by Jonas Basanavičius and Antanas Smetona, declared it independent and democratic, with Vilnius as capital. Real independence came only when Germany lost the war that November, and the new state then had to fight Soviet Russia, Polish forces and others.

Poland seized Vilnius in 1920, and Kaunas served as the temporary capital. The state lasted until the Soviet occupation of 1940. In 1990 the Act of 11 March restored it. See Lithuania.
